scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer quarter-wave stack centered at 300 nm will produce high reflectance in the 200-400 nm UV band while maintaining high transmittance in the 800-1500 nm SWIR band, because the Bragg condition is satisfied at UV wavelengths but not at SWIR wavelengths.
expected_advantages: Quarter-wave seeding should converge faster than unbounded optimization
20 layers provides sufficient reflectance in UV while leaving margin under 30-layer limit
Alternating high/low index structure is a well-known reflector topology
Thickness bounds prevent optimizer from exploring physically unrealistic or manufacturing-difficult thicknesses
known_risks: I am recalling approximate refractive indices for HfO2 and SiO2 in UV; actual values from the material catalog may differ and affect quarter-wave thickness calculations
The quarter-wave condition at 300 nm may not optimally cover the full 200-400 nm band; band edges may have lower reflectance
I am uncertain whether 20 layers is optimal versus 18 or 22; this route fixes 20 and does not explore layer count as a variable
Dispersion of HfO2 and SiO2 across 200-1500 nm may shift the effective quarter-wave condition; I am not modeling dispersion explicitly in this hypothesis
The previous iteration achieved target_score ~0.56; I do not know if this thickness re-seeding will improve that without running the solver
What would settle these uncertainties: measured n/k dispersion data from the material catalog for hfo2 and sio2 across 200-1500 nm, and a layer-count sweep to find optimal pair number
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise compared to iteration 03's 0.5606 if quarter-wave seeding improves convergence
valid_candidates count should remain similar or increase if thickness bounds are physically realizable
tightest_margin should not fall across rounds if the optimizer is finding robust solutions
thicknesses_nm should cluster around 39-40 nm for HfO2 and 50-52 nm for SiO2 if quarter-wave condition is being approached
run_status should remain 'completed' without optimization failures
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, reduce mutation intensity and continue for one more round before stopping
if thicknesses_nm converge to within 1 nm variation across all candidates for three consecutive rounds, stop and keep the current best
